opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Peter says it after many disciples walk away. Jesus has just spoken about the Bread of Life. The teaching is hard. People leave. Jesus turns to the Twelve and asks, “Do you also want to go away?”

Peter answers:

“Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.”

It is not perfect understanding. It is attachment.  He does not say, “I fully grasp this.”

He says, “There is nowhere else.”

That connects directly to the Transfiguration.  On the mountain, the Father says, “Listen to Him.”  After the Bread of Life discourse, Peter says, “You have the words of everlasting life.”

Even when confused.
Even when afraid.
Even when others leave.

Your words, Lord, are Spirit and life.  That means they do not just inform. They sustain. They breathe into what feels dead. They steady when the cross comes into view.

Peter will still deny Him. He will still fail. But he already knows this much: life is not found anywhere else.

And that is enough to stay.

If this line is speaking to you, it may not be because everything makes sense. It may be because, at the bottom of it, you know the same thing:

Where else would you go?
